_meta.provenance: Original fault-code reference prose authored for vibesODB2. General diagnostic guidance only; not a diagnosis of any specific vehicle.

00003.title: Control Module Defective
00003.meaning: Internal memory checksum or hardware self-check failed inside the module.
fixes: Re-verify coding and power feed; if permanent, module repair/replacement is needed

00256.title: A/C Pressure / Temperature Sensor (G395)
00256.meaning: High-pressure refrigerant sensor G395 reports implausible pressure or lost LIN comms (disables A/C compressor).
causes: Corroded 3-pin plug on G395 sensor behind front grille
fixes: Inspect G395 sensor plug near condenser for green corrosion
Have A/C refrigerant static pressure checked

00283.title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor; Front Left (G47)
00283.meaning: Missing or erratic wheel speed signal from front-left hub.
fixes: Inspect front-left sensor cable and bearing encoder ring

00285.title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor; Front Right (G45)
00285.meaning: Missing or erratic wheel speed signal from front-right hub.
causes: Damaged magnetic encoder ring in front-right wheel bearing
fixes: Inspect front-right wheel speed sensor tip and wiring

00287.title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor; Rear Right (G44)
00287.meaning: Missing or erratic wheel speed signal from rear-right hub.
causes: Swollen rusty rear hub bearing magnetic seal
Broken wire along rear trailing arm
fixes: Check rear-right trailing arm cable and inspect sensor tip for rub marks

00290.title: ABS Wheel Speed Sensor; Rear Left (G46)
00290.meaning: Missing or erratic wheel speed signal from rear-left hub.
causes: Swollen rusty rear bearing magnetic ring
Broken wire on rear suspension arm
fixes: Inspect rear-left sensor cable along trailing arm and check bearing ring

00361.title: Heater Element for Auxiliary Heater (Z35)
00361.meaning: Electric PTC cabin heater element inside dash heater box failed internal load test.
causes: Cracked solder joints on heavy MOSFET resistors inside Z35 PTC unit
fixes: Reflow PCB joints or replace Z35 PTC element if instant electric warm air is needed

00446.title: Function Limitation Due to Under-Voltage
00446.meaning: Module disabled outputs temporarily because supply voltage dropped too low.
causes: Weak battery during cranking or prolonged parking
fixes: Charge and test 12V battery

00447.title: Function Limitation Due to Over-Voltage
fixes: Verify alternator output does not exceed 14.8V

00456.title: Control Module for Access and Start Control (J518)
00456.meaning: Fault or missing comms with steering lock / start authorization unit.
fixes: Check steering lock operation and battery voltage

00457.title: Central Electronics Control Module (J519)
00457.meaning: Companion module reports stored fault or missing message from 0x09 Central Electrics.
fixes: Inspect faults inside Address 0x09 directly

00469.title: Infotainment Databus in Single-Wire Mode
00469.meaning: One wire of the Infotainment CAN pair is open or grounded.
causes: Pinched quadlock CAN wire behind stereo
fixes: Pull radio to inspect orange/purple & orange/brown CAN pair behind head unit

00470.title: Comfort CAN Databus in Single-Wire Mode
00470.meaning: One wire of the two-wire Comfort CAN bus is open or shorted; bus is limping on a single wire.
causes: Broken orange/green or orange/brown CAN wire inside rubber door hinge boot
Corroded splice under cab floor mat
fixes: Pull back rubber door bellows on driver and passenger doors to check for snapped CAN wires

00493.title: ESP Sensor Unit (G419)
00493.meaning: Combined yaw-rate & lateral acceleration cluster fault.
fixes: Inspect G419 mounting under seat/console

00526.title: Brake Light Switch (F)
causes: Blown brake lamp fuse or both bulbs out
fixes: Verify brake lights work and inspect switch above brake pedal

00532.title: Supply Voltage B+
00532.meaning: Module detected abnormally low (or interrupted) battery supply voltage.
fixes: Test resting battery voltage (>12.4V); if recorded during battery work, clear and recheck

00562.title: Sensor for Oil Level and Oil Temperature (G266)
00562.meaning: Sump oil level/temperature sensor (TOG) signal missing or shorted (triggers yellow oil sensor warning on dash).
causes: Failed G266 sensor on bottom of sump
Faulty bonnet microswitch preventing oil warning reset
fixes: Inspect 3-pin plug on bottom of oil sump and undertray wiring

00576.title: Terminal 15 Ignition Supply
fixes: Check ignition switch electrical contacts and Terminal 15 relay

00588.title: Airbag Igniter; Driver Side (N95)
00588.meaning: Driver steering-wheel airbag squib resistance is outside safe limits.
causes: Broken ribbon inside steering column clockspring / slip ring
Loose yellow airbag plug behind airbag or column
fixes: CAUTION: Disconnect battery negative for 15 minutes before touching SRS plugs; never probe squibs with a multimeter
Inspect yellow slip-ring connectors; replace clockspring if open circuit

00589.title: Airbag Igniter 1; Passenger Side (N131)
00589.meaning: Passenger dashboard airbag igniter resistance outside tolerance (common if glovebox airbag switch/plug was unplugged with ignition on).
causes: Glovebox passenger airbag switch unplugged while battery was connected!
Loose yellow SRS plug behind glovebox
fixes: Disconnect battery before refitting trim; if caused by unplugging glovebox switch during trim removal, reconnect and clear code

00625.title: Vehicle Speed Signal
00625.meaning: Implausible or missing speed pulse line.
causes: Aftermarket radio wired onto blue/white gala speed wire shorting it!
fixes: If an aftermarket stereo was fitted, disconnect the blue/white speed wire from the ISO harness

00665.title: Boost Pressure Regulation: Control Range Not Reached
00665.meaning: Measured manifold boost fell below target (VAG 5-digit form of P0299).
causes: Split boost hose or intercooler leak
Perished vacuum line to turbo capsule
Sticky N75 valve or VNT vanes
fixes: Check boost hose joints for oil misting and vacuum-test turbo actuator

00668.title: Supply Voltage Terminal 30
00668.meaning: Permanent +12V battery feed dropped below threshold.
fixes: Check battery-top fuse connections and battery charge

00710.title: Defroster Flap Positioning Motor (V107)
00710.meaning: Defrost flap motor failed to reach stop.
fixes: Run Climatronic flap adaptation

00716.title: Air Recirculation Flap Positioning Motor (V113)
00716.meaning: Recirculation flap motor sticking or clicking.
fixes: Replace V113 actuator behind glovebox

00778.title: Steering Angle Sensor (G85)
00778.meaning: Steering angle sensor G85 is uncalibrated or implausible.
fixes: Start engine, turn steering full left, full right, centre, and drive straight ~50 m to re-learn

00779.title: Outside Air Temperature Sensor (G17)
00779.meaning: Ambient bumper temperature sensor G17 is open or shorted.
causes: Unplugged ambient temp sensor behind lower front bumper grille
fixes: Check 2-pin sensor clipped behind lower front grille

00819.title: High Pressure Sensor (G65) — Air Conditioning
00819.meaning: A/C refrigerant pressure sensor G65 signal too low or missing.
causes: Lost A/C gas charge from stone-damaged condenser
Corroded 3-pin plug on A/C high-pressure pipe
fixes: Inspect 3-pin G65 connector on aluminium A/C pipework; check system gas pressure

00856.title: Radio Antenna
00856.meaning: Open circuit or short on powered FM/AM antenna phantom feed (common when fitting aftermarket stereo without phantom adapter).
causes: Aftermarket head unit fitted without Fakra phantom power injector
fixes: Check wing-mirror antenna base for water ingress or fit powered Fakra adapter

00883.title: Ignition Starter Switch (D) Terminal S
00883.meaning: Key-in-ignition 'S-contact' signal implausible (radio may not turn off when key is pulled).
causes: Sticky mechanical/electrical S-contact in ignition barrel
fixes: Lubricate lock cylinder lightly or replace electrical ignition switch block on rear of barrel

00884.title: Ignition Starter Switch (D) Terminal X
00884.meaning: X-relief load-shedding contact implausible (wipers/blower/headlights fail during or after cranking).
fixes: Inspect X-relief relay and ignition switch block

00907.title: Intervention Load Management
00907.meaning: Central Electrics raised idle RPM and shed comfort consumers because battery voltage sagged.
causes: Alternator DF load wire fault (check for 01117)
Heavy camper/leisure draw on starter battery
fixes: Check charging voltage (13.8–14.4V) and inspect alternator 2-pin plug under engine

00912.title: Window Regulator Switch; Front Left (E40)
00912.meaning: Driver electric window switch signal implausible.
causes: Rainwater ingress in driver door switch pack
Broken wire in driver door hinge boot
fixes: Pop out driver window switch pack and clean contacts

00928.title: Locking Module for Central Locking; Driver Side (F220)
00928.meaning: Driver door latch microswitch reported implausible state.
causes: Worn microswitches or dry solder joints inside driver door latch
Broken wire in driver door rubber boot
fixes: Check door hinge wiring boot first, then replace F220 door lock actuator

00929.title: Locking Module for Central Locking; Passenger Side (F221)
00929.meaning: Front passenger door lock unit reported implausible latch/safe feedback.
causes: Broken wire in passenger door boot
fixes: Inspect door jamb wiring gaiter and F221 latch unit

00930.title: Locking Module for Central Locking; Rear Left (F222)
00930.meaning: Rear-left / sliding door lock unit reported implausible feedback (on Transporters often dirty sliding door contact pins!).
causes: Tarnished brass B-pillar contact pins and sprung plungers on sliding door
fixes: Clean sliding door brass contact plate and sprung pins with a fibreglass pencil / contact cleaner first

00931.title: Locking Module for Central Locking; Rear Right (F223)
00931.meaning: Rear-right / sliding door lock unit reported implausible feedback.
causes: Dirty B-pillar sliding door contact pins
fixes: Clean sliding door contact pins and check plunger spring travel

00932.title: Electric Window Motor; Driver Side (V147)
00932.meaning: Driver window motor thermal cutout or Hall pulse fault.
fixes: Hold switch down 2s past bottom, then up 2s past top to relearn pinch limits

00933.title: Electric Window Motor; Passenger Side (V148)
00933.meaning: Passenger window motor or adaptation fault.
fixes: Relearn upper/lower window limits

00978.title: Lamp for Low Beam; Left (M29)
00978.meaning: Left dipped-beam bulb circuit open or shorted.
fixes: Inspect left headlight bulb and 2/3-pin socket for heat discolouration

00979.title: Lamp for Low Beam; Right (M31)
00979.meaning: Right dipped-beam bulb circuit open or shorted.
fixes: Inspect right headlight bulb and connector

00984.title: Left Tail Light Bulb (M4)
00984.meaning: Left rear tail lamp circuit open.
causes: Corroded rear light cluster bulb tray or trailer socket
fixes: Check left tail bulb and inspect rear light cluster earth track for corrosion

00985.title: Right Tail Light Bulb (M2)
00985.meaning: Right rear tail lamp circuit open.
fixes: Check right tail bulb and holder contacts

00987.title: Lamp for Brake Light; Left (M9)
fixes: Replace bulb and clean cluster contacts

00988.title: Lamp for Brake Light; Right (M10)
fixes: Replace bulb and clean cluster contacts

01044.title: Control Module Incorrectly Coded
01044.meaning: Long coding or gateway installation list conflicts with actual connected hardware.
causes: Feature enabled in coding for hardware not present on vehicle
Replacement module not coded to vehicle
fixes: Review recent coding changes or restore saved pre-write backup

01117.title: Generator Terminal DF Load Signal
01117.meaning: Alternator DF load feedback wire to Central Electrics / ECU is open or implausible (classic Transporter T5 broken wire fault).
causes: Snapped thin blue/brown wire inside corrugated conduit near starter motor / gearbox bracket
fixes: Open the plastic conduit beneath the starter/gearbox mount and check the thin alternator sense wires for a clean break
Verify 14V charging output at battery

01134.title: Alarm Horn (H12)
01134.meaning: Backup alarm sounder H12 missing on LIN bus or defective.
causes: Failed internal battery inside H12 siren
fixes: Check alarm siren fuse and H12 unit under scuttle / wheel arch

01135.title: Interior Monitoring Sensors
01135.meaning: Ultrasonic cabin motion sensor module unplugged or faulty (common in campervan roof-lining conversions).
causes: Overhead console ultrasonic sensor left unplugged after headlining / pop-top work
fixes: Reconnect overhead sensor or disable interior monitoring if permanently removed for camper conversion

01176.title: Key — Transponder Signal Too Low
01176.meaning: Immobilizer reader coil around ignition barrel read a weak or invalid key transponder.
causes: Damaged glass RFID transponder capsule in dropped key
Poor connection on ignition barrel reader coil plug
fixes: Test with spare key first to isolate key vs reader coil

01206.title: Signal for Duration of Ignition Off Time
01206.meaning: HVAC lost real-time clock reference from instrument cluster after power loss.
fixes: Clear code after setting clock; should not return with healthy battery

01217.title: Side Airbag Igniter; Driver Side (N199)
01217.meaning: Driver seat side-airbag squib resistance out of range.
causes: Yellow SRS plug disturbed under driver seat
fixes: Disconnect battery for 15 minutes, reseat yellow plug under driver seat, then clear fault

01218.title: Side Airbag Igniter; Passenger Side (N200)
01218.meaning: Passenger seat side-airbag squib resistance out of range.
causes: Yellow SRS plug disturbed under passenger seat / swivel base
fixes: Disconnect battery for 15 minutes, check under-seat yellow SRS connector, then clear fault

01221.title: Crash Sensor Side Airbag; Driver Side (G179)
01221.meaning: Open circuit or wrong sensor on driver door/B-pillar side impact sensor (very common broken wire in door boot!).
causes: Snapped wire inside driver door rubber accordion gaiter
fixes: Disconnect battery 15 min, pull back driver door rubber boot, and check for broken sensor wires

01222.title: Crash Sensor Side Airbag; Passenger Side (G180)
01222.meaning: Fault in passenger side impact crash sensor circuit.
causes: Broken wire in passenger door hinge boot
fixes: Disconnect battery 15 min and inspect passenger door hinge wiring

01259.title: Fuel Pump Relay (J17)
01259.meaning: Open or short in electric fuel pump relay control.
fixes: Test/swap fuel pump relay and check fuse

01271.title: Positioning Motor for Temperature Flap (V68)
01271.meaning: Cabin blend-air temperature flap motor jammed or noisy.
causes: Worn potentiometer inside V68 flap motor
fixes: Run HVAC adaptation or replace V68 motor

01272.title: Positioning Motor for Central Flap (V70)
fixes: Run HVAC flap basic setting

01274.title: Air Flow Flap Positioning Motor (V71)
01274.meaning: Fresh/recirculation flap motor V71 jammed or worn.
causes: Stripped nylon cog inside V71 motor behind glovebox
fixes: Replace V71 actuator behind glovebox

01279.title: Longitudinal Acceleration Sensor (G251)
01279.meaning: Longitudinal G-sensor out of calibration or faulty.
fixes: Calibrate on level ground

01299.title: Diagnostic Interface for Data Bus (J533 / Gateway)
01299.meaning: Companion module flags a stored fault or coding mismatch in 0x19 Gateway.
fixes: Check Address 0x19 CAN Gateway directly

01304.title: Radio (R) — No Signal / Communication
01304.meaning: CAN Gateway expects factory radio on Infotainment CAN, but none responded (routine when an aftermarket stereo is fitted).
causes: Aftermarket stereo installed without CANbus interface
fixes: Harmless if aftermarket head unit is fitted; otherwise check radio quadlock fuse

01305.title: Databus for Infotainment
fixes: Inspect quadlock CAN connections

01309.title: Power Steering Control Module (J500)
01309.meaning: Fault stored in or lost comms with 0x44 Steering Assist.
fixes: Scan Address 0x44

01312.title: Powertrain Data Bus
01312.meaning: Fault detected on high-speed Powertrain CAN.
fixes: Inspect Engine and ABS connectors

01314.title: Engine Control Module (ECM) — Check DTC Memory / No Comms
01314.meaning: Either CAN comms to 0x01 Engine dropped out, or 0x01 has an active fault stored.
causes: Active fault stored inside 0x01 Engine ECU
Failing main ECM power relay (J317 / Relay 109) if 'No Communication'
fixes: Check status symptom: 'Check DTC Memory' means read 0x01 Engine first; 'No Communication' means check ECM relay and fuses

01315.title: Transmission Control Module — No Comms / Fault Stored
01315.meaning: Gateway or ABS lost comms with 0x02 Gearbox or reports a stored gearbox fault.
fixes: Check Address 0x02 faults and mechatronic power supply

01316.title: ABS Brake Control Module — No Comms / Fault Stored
01316.meaning: Missing communication or active fault flagged by 0x03 ABS.
causes: Blown ABS strip fuse on battery top
fixes: Scan 0x03 ABS directly and inspect battery-top strip fuses

01317.title: Control Module in Instrument Cluster (J285)
01317.meaning: Lost communication or fault stored in 0x17 Instrument Cluster.
causes: Cracked cluster header pins on older clusters
fixes: Check 0x17 Instrument Cluster faults and connector latch

01320.title: Control Module for Climatronic (J255)
01320.meaning: Missing comms or fault stored in 0x08 HVAC.
causes: Unplugged dash fascia during stereo work
fixes: Check 0x08 Climate Control

01321.title: Control Module for Airbags (J234)
01321.meaning: Lost communication with 0x15 SRS Airbag module.
causes: Unplugged airbag module under centre console
fixes: Check fuse supply to SRS module

01325.title: Control Module for Tire Pressure Monitoring (J502)
01325.meaning: No communication with direct TPMS receiver.
causes: Unplugged TPMS module or coding mismatch
fixes: Check TPMS fuse or Gateway coding

01330.title: Central Control Module for Central Convenience (J393)
01330.meaning: No communication or stored fault in comfort module.
causes: Water ingress under cab floor carpet
fixes: Check under-seat / under-carpet module housing for dampness

01331.title: Door Control Module; Driver Side (J386)
01331.meaning: Lost communication or fault in driver door module.
causes: Snapped power or CAN wire inside driver door hinge boot
fixes: Inspect driver door rubber wiring boot

01332.title: Door Control Module; Passenger Side (J387)
01332.meaning: Lost communication or fault in passenger door module.
causes: Broken wire in passenger door hinge boot
fixes: Inspect passenger door rubber wiring boot

01333.title: Door Control Module; Rear Left (J388)
01333.meaning: Lost communication with rear-left door module.
causes: Broken wire in rear door boot
fixes: Inspect rear-left door wiring gaiter

01334.title: Door Control Module; Rear Right (J389)
01334.meaning: Lost communication with rear-right door module.
causes: Broken wire in rear door boot
fixes: Inspect rear-right door wiring gaiter

01336.title: Comfort CAN Databus Fault / Single-Wire
01336.meaning: Comfort CAN twisted pair operating in single-wire fallback or faulted.
causes: Snapped CAN wire inside door rubber accordion boot
fixes: Inspect wiring inside front door rubber bellows

01406.title: No Flame — Auxiliary / Parking Heater
01406.meaning: Diesel auxiliary heater (Webasto Thermo Top) failed to establish flame during startup.
causes: Air in heater fuel line because fuel tank was below 1/4 reserve
Locked-out heater after repeated failed starts
fixes: Ensure fuel tank is above 1/4 full; inspect metering pump click and burner chamber

01410.title: Heater Over-Temp — Auxiliary Heater
01410.meaning: Webasto auxiliary heater shut down on overheat.
causes: Failed V55 electric circulation pump (check for 01415)
fixes: Verify electric coolant pump runs when heater starts

01414.title: Combustion Air Blower (V6) — Auxiliary Heater
01414.meaning: Combustion fan inside underfloor Webasto auxiliary heater stalled or out of speed range (very common dry PCB solder joints).
causes: Cracked solder joints on underfloor heater control PCB
fixes: Inspect underfloor auxiliary heater module under left cab floor; PCB reflow or blower replacement resolves

01415.title: Recirculating Pump (V55) — Auxiliary Heater
01415.meaning: Electric coolant circulation pump on auxiliary heater open or seized (causes heater overheat shutdown).
causes: Worn brushes / seized impeller in V55 auxiliary coolant pump
fixes: Replace V55 electric coolant pump mounted beside underfloor heater

01423.title: Lateral Acceleration Sensor (G200)
causes: Dry solder joints in G200 sensor
fixes: Check G200 mounting and live lateral acceleration reading on level ground

01435.title: Brake Pressure Sensor 1 (G201)
01435.meaning: Hydraulic brake line pressure sensor inside ABS unit reads implausible pressure at rest.
causes: Internal G201 transducer failure inside ABS hydraulic block
fixes: Verify live brake pressure reads ~0 bar with foot off pedal; internal G201 failure can be repaired with ABS pump rebuild

01494.title: Bulb for Parking Lamp; Left (M1)
fixes: Replace sidelight bulb or check holder contacts

01498.title: Bulb for Parking Lamp; Right (M3)
fixes: Replace right sidelight bulb

01504.title: Bulb for License Plate Light (X)
01504.meaning: Number-plate lamp circuit open (extremely common tailgate corrosion point on Transporters).
causes: Water-corroded brass contacts inside tailgate/barn-door number plate lamp plinth
fixes: Unscrew rear number-plate lamp lenses and check for green verdigris corrosion inside the grab-handle strip

01516.title: Terminal 30; Left
01516.meaning: Missing permanent +12V on one of BCM's fused supply rails.
causes: Blown cab fuse feeding left BCM output bank
fixes: Check cab fusebox fuses feeding Central Electrics

01598.title: Drive Battery Voltage
01598.meaning: Supply voltage at Central Electrics fell below lower threshold.
fixes: Check resting (>12.4V) and running (13.8–14.4V) battery voltage

01800.title: Light Switch (E1) — Implausible Signal
01800.meaning: Rotary headlight switch E1 returned an invalid contact combination.
fixes: Push rotary switch in at '0' and twist clockwise to slide switch out; inspect plug or test without aftermarket auto-light box

02067.title: Optical Databus (MOST) Unauthorized Awakening / Break
fixes: Fit MOST optical bypass loop if removing an unused module

02251.title: Heater Unit Locked — Auxiliary Heater
02251.meaning: Diesel auxiliary heater entered safety lockout after repeated flame-outs or overheats.
causes: Repeated low-fuel airlocks, failed V55 water pump (01415), or failed glow pin
fixes: Fix underlying pump/fuel fault before unlocking heater

02252.title: Generator (Alternator) — No Communication
02252.meaning: ECU/Gateway lost LIN communication with smart alternator regulator.
causes: Broken single LIN wire to alternator plug (common under-engine chafe on T5.1/T6)
fixes: Inspect single-wire/2-pin plug on back of alternator and trace under sump

02391.title: Terminal 30 Reference
02391.meaning: Missing reference +12V fuse input to BCM.
causes: Blown BCM reference fuse in dash fusebox
fixes: Check all BCM supply fuses

02399.title: Control Circuit for Terminal 30
02399.meaning: Interior lighting / saver relay Terminal 30g shorted (often caused by pinched interior LED/camper wiring!).
causes: Pinched wire under roof lining or sunvisor vanity light screw
fixes: Check interior dome lights and any campervan 12V roof wiring tapped into courtesy circuit

02479.title: Partial Consumer Shut-Off Active
02479.meaning: Energy manager switched off comfort loads to protect starting capability.
fixes: Charge and test starter battery

03158.title: Information Electronics Control Module 1 (J794 / 5F)
03158.meaning: Fault stored in or missing comms with 5F MIB infotainment unit.
fixes: Check infotainment unit status

03405.title: Bass Speaker Rear / Door Open Circuit
causes: Broken speaker wire in door boot
fixes: Test speaker resistance across quadlock audio pins

B104A.title: Rain / Light Recognition Sensor Fault
B104A.meaning: BCM lost LIN communication or detected a circuit fault on the windscreen rain/light sensor (G397).
causes: Rain/light sensor unplugged behind interior mirror trim after windscreen replacement
Rain/light sensor coded as installed on a van without one
fixes: Check 3-pin connector behind rearview mirror trim
Verify 12V, ground, and violet/white LIN wire
If vehicle has manual wipers only, untick Rain/Light Sensor in BCM coding

B1087.title: LIN Bus Air Conditioning / Flap Motor Communication
B1087.meaning: HVAC module lost communication with one or more LIN-bus air distribution flap motors.
causes: One shorted flap motor pulling down the daisy-chained LIN line
fixes: Inspect HVAC flap motor connectors behind glovebox / centre console

B108C.title: Left Temperature Flap Motor Jammed / Fault
B108C.meaning: Left blend-air flap actuator V158 failed to reach its calibrated end stops.
causes: Worn feedback track or stripped gear inside V158 actuator
fixes: Run HVAC flap end-stop adaptation or replace V158 motor above driver footwell

B1090.title: Defrost Flap Positioning Motor Fault
B1090.meaning: Windscreen defrost flap motor V107 is sticking or out of calibration.
fixes: Check actuator movement under dash while switching to windscreen demist

B109E.title: Air Recirculation Flap Motor Fault
B109E.meaning: Fresh/recirculation air flap actuator V113 jammed or missed end stop.
causes: Stripped plastic gear inside V113 motor behind glovebox (very common clicking noise on ignition on)
fixes: Listen for rhythmic clicking behind glovebox; replace V113 recirculation motor

B10A4.title: Fresh Air Blower Front Fault
B10A4.meaning: Cabin heater blower motor V2 or its PWM regulator J126 reported a fault or mechanical bind.
causes: Dry/rusted blower fan bearings after scuttle water ingress
fixes: Drop blower motor behind passenger footwell to check free spin and inspect cabin filter

B10B3.title: Functional Restriction of Seat Heating
B10B3.meaning: Heated seat output reduced or shut off due to load management or thermistor fault.
causes: Broken seat heater pad wire or NTC sensor in seat base
fixes: Measure seat cushion NTC thermistor resistance under seat plug

B10CD.title: Function Limitation Due to Energy Management
B10CD.meaning: Gateway / BCM shed non-essential comfort loads because battery state of charge fell low.
fixes: Charge battery with an AGM-capable smart charger and test parasitic draw if recurring

B1148.title: Terminal 15 Ignition Switch / Relay Implausible
B1148.meaning: Mismatch between ignition switch Terminal 15 input and main Terminal 15 relay output.
fixes: Inspect ignition switch electrical block and Terminal 15 relay under dash

B1168.title: Steering Angle Sensor (G85) No Basic Setting / Implausible
B1168.meaning: Steering angle sensor G85 has lost zero calibration or failed.
fixes: Turn wheel full lock left to right with engine running and drive straight a short distance

B1217.title: Side Airbag Igniter Driver Side Resistance
B1217.meaning: Driver seat thorax airbag circuit impedance is outside safe bounds.
causes: Loose yellow airbag connector under driver seat (common on swivel/adjustable van seats)
fixes: Disconnect battery negative for 15 minutes before inspecting under-seat yellow connector—never probe airbag pins with a multimeter

B1218.title: Side Airbag Igniter Passenger Side Resistance
B1218.meaning: Passenger seat/bench side airbag or occupancy/pretensioner circuit resistance out of range.
causes: Unplugged or strained yellow connector under passenger seat / swivel base
fixes: Disconnect battery for 15 minutes, reseat and secure under-seat yellow harness plug, then clear SRS faults

B122D.title: Lock Unit for Central Locking Fault
B122D.meaning: Door latch microswitch reported implausible locked/safe state.
causes: Worn microswitch or cracked solder joints inside door lock module
Broken wire inside rubber door-frame gaiter
fixes: Inspect wiring inside rubber door hinge boot first, then replace door lock mechanism

B131F.title: Alarm Horn (H12) No Communication / Defective
B131F.meaning: Backup battery-sounder siren H12 failed self-test or lost LIN comms.
causes: Internal NiMH backup battery leaked onto H12 siren PCB (common on 8+ year old vehicles)
fixes: Inspect H12 siren under wheel-arch liner / scuttle and check dedicated siren fuse

B1479.title: Remote Key Battery Voltage Low
B1479.meaning: Key fob transmitted a low-battery flag during unlock/lock.
causes: Weak CR2025 / CR2032 coin cell in key fob
fixes: Replace coin cell in remote key fob

B2000.title: Control Module Defective (Internal Checksum / Hardware)
B2000.meaning: Module failed an internal ROM/EEPROM checksum or self-test.
causes: Corrupted internal flash/EEPROM from voltage drop
fixes: Check supply voltage stability; persistent B2000 normally requires module repair or replacement

B2010.title: No Basic Setting
B2010.meaning: Module or actuator requires end-stop / zero-point basic calibration before operating.
causes: New part fitted or battery/coding reset without completing basic setting
fixes: Perform the required calibration procedure for the replaced actuator/sensor

C101A.title: Front Left ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Fault
C101A.meaning: Signal missing, erratic, or open on front-left wheel speed sensor.
causes: Swollen/cracked magnetic encoder ring on wheel bearing
Chafed sensor wire in front wheel arch
fixes: Inspect sensor wire routing at strut bracket and check bearing magnetic ring face for rust

C101B.title: Front Right ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Fault
C101B.meaning: Signal missing, erratic, or open on front-right wheel speed sensor.
causes: Damaged magnetic ABS ring in wheel bearing
fixes: Inspect front-right ABS sensor and bearing magnetic seal

C101C.title: Rear Left ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Fault
C101C.meaning: Signal missing, erratic, or open on rear-left wheel speed sensor (common rust swell point on Transporters).
causes: Rust under sensor bracket pushing sensor away or scraping magnetic bearing ring
fixes: Remove rear-left sensor and inspect tip for rub marks against a swollen bearing ring

C101D.title: Rear Right ABS Wheel Speed Sensor Fault
C101D.meaning: Signal missing, erratic, or open on rear-right wheel speed sensor.
causes: Corroded magnetic ring on rear hub bearing
fixes: Inspect rear-right trailing arm cable and sensor tip for contact wear

C10AC.title: Steering End Stops Not Learned
C10AC.meaning: Electro-mechanical steering assist requires left/right full-lock end-stop adaptation.
fixes: With engine idling, turn wheel smoothly to full left lock, hold 2 seconds, then full right lock, hold 2 seconds, and centre

P0011.title: Camshaft Position Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
P0011.meaning: Intake camshaft phase did not return to target angle as commanded.
causes: Low engine oil level or dirty oil clogging VVT spool valve
fixes: Check engine oil level and service history
Inspect and clean VVT oil control screen/solenoid

P0012.title: Camshaft Position Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)
P0012.meaning: Intake cam stayed retarded relative to target.
fixes: Check oil level/condition and VVT solenoid

P0016.title: Crankshaft – Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
P0016.meaning: Phase angle between crankshaft sensor G28 and camshaft sensor G40 is outside mechanical tolerance.
causes: Stretched timing chain or worn tensioner
Timing belt jumped a tooth or set without locking tools
fixes: Check live camshaft torsion / phase adaptation angle before driving further
Physically verify mechanical timing marks with locking pins

P0017.title: Crankshaft – Exhaust Camshaft Correlation (Bank 1)
P0017.meaning: Exhaust camshaft timing out of phase with crank.
fixes: Verify mechanical timing marks

P0030.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0030.meaning: Open or short in upstream lambda sensor heater.
fixes: Check engine bay O2 heater fuse and measure heater pins (~3–10 Ω)

P0036.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0036.meaning: Open or short in downstream lambda sensor heater.
fixes: Inspect underbody O2 cable and heater resistance

P0068.title: Manifold Pressure / Mass Airflow Throttle Correlation
P0068.meaning: Measured intake manifold pressure and airflow disagree with the throttle valve angle.
causes: Unmetered air leak after the MAF sensor
Carbon fouling around the throttle plate
Drifted MAP or MAF sensor reading
fixes: Smoke-test intake hoses and intercooler joints for leaks
Clean throttle body bore and re-run throttle basic adaptation
Compare key-on engine-off MAP reading against atmospheric pressure

P0087.title: Fuel Rail / System Pressure Too Low
P0087.meaning: High-pressure common-rail sensor (G247) measured rail pressure significantly below target.
causes: Clogged fuel filter starving the lift/high-pressure pump
Failed in-tank or inline auxiliary electric fuel pump
Sticking N290 fuel metering valve or N276 rail pressure regulator
Excessive injector back-leakage or HPFP wear
fixes: Inspect fuel filter bowl for metallic swarf before running further
Replace fuel filter if overdue and prime fuel system before cranking
Perform injector return leak-off bottle test
Verify low-pressure lift pump delivery pressure

P0088.title: Fuel Rail / System Pressure Too High
P0088.meaning: Common-rail fuel pressure spiked above the commanded safety ceiling.
causes: Sticking N276 rail pressure regulating valve
Sticking N290 fuel volume metering valve on HPFP
fixes: Inspect wiring and connectors on N276 (rail end) and N290 (pump)
Check rail pressure reading at key-on engine-off (should read near 0 bar)

P0089.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Performance
P0089.meaning: Rail pressure regulator duty cycle reached control limits while trying to maintain target pressure.
causes: Air ingress in low-pressure fuel lines
fixes: Check transparent/low-pressure supply lines for air bubbles
Inspect fuel filter and regulating valve connectors

P0090.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Control Circuit Open
P0090.meaning: Open circuit on fuel metering / rail pressure solenoid.
fixes: Check 2-pin connector on high-pressure fuel pump

P0091.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Control Circuit Low
P0091.meaning: Short to ground on fuel pressure control valve.
causes: Chafed wire on fuel rail / HPFP
fixes: Inspect HPFP and rail regulator wiring

P0092.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Control Circuit High
P0092.meaning: Short to battery positive on fuel pressure regulator.
fixes: Check regulator harness continuity

P0100.title: Mass Air Flow (MAF) Sensor Circuit Fault
P0100.meaning: Electrical open, short, or missing signal from the intake mass airflow sensor (G70).
causes: Unplugged MAF connector after air filter service
Broken 5V reference, 12V supply, or signal wire near airbox
fixes: Check that the MAF multi-plug is seated and locked
Verify supply voltage and ground at the MAF harness plug
Inspect wiring back to the engine harness conduit for chafing

P0101.title: Mass Air Flow (MAF) Range / Performance
P0101.meaning: Airflow reported by sensor G70 does not match expected volumetric flow for the current RPM and boost.
causes: Oil mist or dust contaminating the MAF sensing element
Split intake pipe between MAF and turbo inlet
Sticking EGR valve altering fresh air intake
fixes: Inspect intake ducting downstream of the MAF for splits or loose clips
Clean sensor element with dedicated MAF cleaner spray without touching the film
Compare specified vs actual MAF in live data under load

P0102.title: Mass Air Flow (MAF) Signal Too Low
P0102.meaning: MAF sensor output voltage or frequency fell below the minimum threshold.
causes: Open circuit or short to ground on MAF signal wire
Disconnected intake hose bypassing the MAF
fixes: Check MAF connector pins and supply fuse
Ensure turbo inlet hose is clamped securely to the MAF housing
Test live airflow reading at idle

P0103.title: Mass Air Flow (MAF) Signal Too High
P0103.meaning: MAF sensor output exceeded the upper plausible limit.
fixes: Inspect MAF plug for moisture or corroded terminals
Check signal wire for short to power
Replace MAF sensor if wiring checks clean

P0106.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) Range / Performance
P0106.meaning: Boost / manifold pressure sensor (G31) reading is implausible compared to barometric pressure or engine load.
causes: Oil-soaked or failed MAP sensor in intercooler pipe
Pinched harness on the front charge pipe
fixes: With ignition ON and engine OFF, check that MAP matches barometric pressure within ~3 kPa
Remove and inspect G31 sensor O-ring and sensing port
Inspect wiring near the radiator fan shroud for rubbing

P0107.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) Circuit Low
P0107.meaning: MAP sensor signal voltage is below minimum (short to ground or open 5V reference).
causes: Broken wire at the G31 charge-pipe plug
5V sensor reference rail pulled low by another sensor
fixes: Tug-test the 4-pin connector on the intercooler pipework
Measure 5V reference and ground at the unplugged connector
Replace G31 sensor if wiring is intact

P0108.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure (MAP) Circuit High
P0108.meaning: MAP sensor signal voltage is stuck near the upper rail.
fixes: Check ground continuity on the MAP harness plug
Inspect connector pins for spread or corrosion
Replace MAP sensor if key-on engine-off pressure reads stuck high

P0112.title: Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Circuit Low
P0112.meaning: IAT sensor resistance is abnormally low, indicating an implausibly hot intake temperature.
causes: IAT signal wire shorted to ground
Failed NTC thermistor inside MAF/MAP combo sensor
fixes: Check live intake temperature on a cold engine against ambient
Inspect sensor harness for pinched insulation

P0113.title: Intake Air Temperature (IAT) Circuit High
P0113.meaning: IAT circuit reads open (commonly ~-40°C in live data).
causes: Unplugged combined MAF/IAT or MAP/IAT connector
fixes: Confirm live IAT reading; -40°C points to an open wire or unplugged sensor
Inspect connector terminals and harness bend right behind the plug

P0115.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Circuit
P0115.meaning: Electrical fault in ECT sensor G62.
fixes: Inspect G62 plug on cylinder head flange

P0116.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Range / Performance
P0116.meaning: Coolant temperature sensor G62 rises too slowly or reads implausibly.
causes: Thermostat stuck open (van runs cool on motorway)
fixes: Monitor live coolant temperature from cold start to warm cruise; should climb steadily to ~88–92°C

P0117.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0117.meaning: G62 resistance is shorted low (reads abnormally hot).
causes: Coolant wicked into G62 connector shorting pins
fixes: Unplug G62 and inspect plug cavity for pink coolant crust

P0118.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0118.meaning: G62 circuit is open (typically shows -40°C and runs radiator fans at full speed).
causes: Broken wire or unlatched plug on cylinder head coolant flange
fixes: Check live coolant temp; if -40°C, bridge or test harness continuity and replace G62 with a fresh O-ring

P0121.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor A Range / Performance
P0121.meaning: Throttle valve feedback disagrees with expected opening.
causes: Oily soot jamming anti-shudder / throttle flap gears
fixes: Inspect throttle body gear housing for oil ingress (common when shaft seal wears)

P0122.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0122.meaning: Throttle position track A below minimum voltage.
fixes: Inspect J338 throttle connector

P0123.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0123.meaning: Throttle position track A above maximum voltage.
fixes: Check ground wire on J338 plug

P0128.title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature
P0128.meaning: Engine failed to reach operating temperature within expected warm-up time.
causes: Main thermostat or DSG inline thermostat stuck open
fixes: Replace stuck thermostat (on DSG vans check the small inline gearbox thermostat first—very common culprit)

P0130.title: O2 Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0130.meaning: Electrical fault on upstream wideband lambda sensor.
causes: Damaged O2 harness on exhaust heatshield
fixes: Inspect 6-pin wideband lambda connector

P0135.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0135.meaning: Upstream O2 sensor heater did not reach operating temperature.
fixes: Check heater supply voltage and coil resistance

P0141.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
fixes: Inspect post-cat O2 wiring

P0171.title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P0171.meaning: Long-term fuel trim added excessive fuel to compensate for lean exhaust.
fixes: Smoke-test intake and check PCV valve membrane

P0172.title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
P0172.meaning: Fuel trim pulled significant fuel due to rich mixture.
causes: Leaking injector or HPFP seal into sump
fixes: Smell engine oil dipstick for fuel contamination and check charge hoses

P0183.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0183.meaning: Fuel temperature sensor G81 circuit is open.
causes: Unplugged 2-pin G81 plug on diesel return/supply line
fixes: Inspect 2-pin G81 plug on fuel lines atop engine

P0190.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0190.meaning: General electrical fault on G247 rail pressure sensor.
fixes: Inspect 3-pin rail sensor connector

P0191.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Range / Performance
P0191.meaning: Rail pressure sensor G247 reports an implausible pressure at rest or during transients.
causes: Drifted G247 sensor on fuel rail
Poor terminal tension in 3-pin rail sensor plug
fixes: Verify live rail pressure reads ~0 bar with engine off
Inspect 3-pin G247 plug for oil/diesel contamination

P0192.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P0192.meaning: G247 rail pressure signal voltage dropped below minimum.
causes: Short to ground on G247 signal or 5V reference
fixes: Measure 5V reference at unplugged G247 connector
Inspect engine top harness for chafing under acoustic cover

P0193.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P0193.meaning: G247 rail pressure signal voltage is open or shorted high.
causes: Broken ground wire at fuel rail plug
fixes: Ensure G247 connector on the fuel rail is fully seated
Test ground and signal continuity on the 3-pin plug

P0201.title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Open / Fault
P0201.meaning: Open circuit or electrical drive fault detected on fuel injector 1.
causes: Loose or heat-brittle terminal on injector 1 plug
fixes: Inspect injector 1 connector pins (and internal head loom on PD engines)
Check injector resistance/capacitance per engine type—never pierce piezo injector wires with power on

P0202.title: Cylinder 2 Injector Circuit Open / Fault
P0202.meaning: Open circuit or electrical drive fault detected on fuel injector 2.
causes: Loose or heat-brittle terminal on injector 2 plug
fixes: Inspect injector 2 connector pins (and internal head loom on PD engines)
Check injector resistance/capacitance per engine type—never pierce piezo injector wires with power on

P0203.title: Cylinder 3 Injector Circuit Open / Fault
P0203.meaning: Open circuit or electrical drive fault detected on fuel injector 3.
causes: Loose or heat-brittle terminal on injector 3 plug
fixes: Inspect injector 3 connector pins (and internal head loom on PD engines)
Check injector resistance/capacitance per engine type—never pierce piezo injector wires with power on

P0204.title: Cylinder 4 Injector Circuit Open / Fault
P0204.meaning: Open circuit or electrical drive fault detected on fuel injector 4.
causes: Loose or heat-brittle terminal on injector 4 plug
fixes: Inspect injector 4 connector pins (and internal head loom on PD engines)
Check injector resistance/capacitance per engine type—never pierce piezo injector wires with power on

P0217.title: Engine Coolant Overtemperature Condition
fixes: Check coolant level once cooled and verify water pump return flow into header tank

P0219.title: Engine Overspeed Condition
P0219.meaning: Engine RPM exceeded rev limiter (typically mechanical downshift over-rev).
causes: Missed downshift driving wheels faster than redline
fixes: Inspect valve train noise if severe over-rev occurred

P0222.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P0222.meaning: Secondary throttle/pedal track voltage too low.
causes: Moisture in pedal or throttle plug
fixes: Inspect throttle and pedal connectors

P0223.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P0223.meaning: Secondary throttle/pedal track voltage too high.
fixes: Check sensor ground continuity

P0234.title: Turbocharger Overboost Condition
P0234.meaning: Actual manifold boost pressure rose significantly above the ECU target map, often triggering limp mode.
causes: Carbon-seized VNT turbocharger vanes sticking in high-boost position
Failed N75 boost control solenoid valve
fixes: Check smooth travel of the turbo VNT actuator linkage over its full stroke
Test N75 vacuum solenoid operation and vent filter
Log requested vs actual boost on a 3rd-gear pull

P0236.title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Range / Performance
P0236.meaning: Charge pressure sensor G31 disagrees with atmospheric pressure before startup or drifts under load.
causes: Chafed wiring loom under battery tray or front slam panel
fixes: Compare boost pressure and barometric sensors with engine off
Inspect front bumper/charge-pipe loom for water ingress

P0237.title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit Low
P0237.meaning: Boost sensor G31 voltage dropped below the lower electrical limit.
causes: Broken wire or short to ground at G31 plug
fixes: Test 5V reference and ground at G31 connector
Repair damaged terminals on intercooler sensor plug

P0238.title: Turbocharger Boost Sensor A Circuit High
P0238.meaning: Boost sensor G31 voltage exceeded the upper electrical limit.
fixes: Verify sensor ground continuity
Replace G31 sensor if wiring tests clean

P0243.title: Turbocharger Wastegate / Boost Solenoid A Malfunction
P0243.meaning: Electrical fault in the N75 boost pressure control solenoid circuit.
fixes: Measure N75 coil resistance (typically ~14–20 Ω)
Verify 12V supply at the N75 plug with ignition on

P0245.title: Turbocharger Boost Solenoid A Low
P0245.meaning: N75 boost solenoid control circuit is open or shorted to ground.
causes: Blown fuse feeding engine bay solenoids
fixes: Check engine bay fuse feeding emissions/boost solenoids
Inspect N75 2-pin plug and pigtail

P0263.title: Cylinder 1 Contribution / Balance Fault
P0263.meaning: Crankshaft speed variation shows cylinder 1 is contributing less torque than adjacent cylinders.
causes: Clogged or worn nozzle on injector 1
Dual-mass flywheel rattle skewing smooth-running calculation at idle
fixes: Compare idle smooth-running / injection quantity deviation across cylinders
Run compression test if injector swap does not move the fault

P0266.title: Cylinder 2 Contribution / Balance Fault
P0266.meaning: Crankshaft speed variation shows cylinder 2 is contributing less torque than adjacent cylinders.
causes: Clogged or worn nozzle on injector 2
Dual-mass flywheel rattle skewing smooth-running calculation at idle
fixes: Compare idle smooth-running / injection quantity deviation across cylinders
Run compression test if injector swap does not move the fault

P0269.title: Cylinder 3 Contribution / Balance Fault
P0269.meaning: Crankshaft speed variation shows cylinder 3 is contributing less torque than adjacent cylinders.
causes: Clogged or worn nozzle on injector 3
Dual-mass flywheel rattle skewing smooth-running calculation at idle
fixes: Compare idle smooth-running / injection quantity deviation across cylinders
Run compression test if injector swap does not move the fault

P0272.title: Cylinder 4 Contribution / Balance Fault
P0272.meaning: Crankshaft speed variation shows cylinder 4 is contributing less torque than adjacent cylinders.
causes: Clogged or worn nozzle on injector 4
Dual-mass flywheel rattle skewing smooth-running calculation at idle
fixes: Compare idle smooth-running / injection quantity deviation across cylinders
Run compression test if injector swap does not move the fault

P0299.title: Turbocharger / Supercharger Underboost
P0299.meaning: Measured manifold boost stayed well below the ECU's requested pressure.
causes: Split rubber boost hose or blown-off O-ring clip joint
Perished vacuum hose to turbo actuator or perforated actuator diaphragm
Weak N75 solenoid or sticking VNT vanes
fixes: Pressure- or smoke-test the charge-air tract from turbo outlet to inlet manifold
Apply hand vacuum pump to the turbo actuator—verify it holds ~18 inHg without leaking down
Inspect thin braided/rubber vacuum lines across the rocker cover and bulkhead
Check N75 solenoid vacuum output at idle

P0300.title: Random / Multiple Cylinder Misfire
P0300.meaning: Crankshaft angular velocity fluctuations indicate misfires across more than one cylinder.
causes: Worn spark plugs or failing coil packs (TSI/TFSI)
Intake vacuum leak or split PCV membrane
Contaminated fuel or low fuel rail pressure
fixes: Check cylinder misfire counters in live data to isolate affected cylinders
Inspect PCV breather valve and intake hoses for air leaks
Verify fuel pressure under load

P0301.title: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
P0301.meaning: Combustion misfire counted above threshold on cylinder 1.
causes: Failing ignition coil or fouled spark plug on cylinder 1 (petrol)
Low mechanical compression or burnt valve
fixes: Swap ignition coil from cylinder 1 to another cylinder to see if the code follows
Inspect spark plug / injector sealing washer
Perform compression test if misfire stays on the same cylinder

P0302.title: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
P0302.meaning: Combustion misfire counted above threshold on cylinder 2.
causes: Failing ignition coil or fouled spark plug on cylinder 2 (petrol)
Low mechanical compression or burnt valve
fixes: Swap ignition coil from cylinder 2 to another cylinder to see if the code follows
Inspect spark plug / injector sealing washer
Perform compression test if misfire stays on the same cylinder

P0303.title: Cylinder 3 Misfire Detected
P0303.meaning: Combustion misfire counted above threshold on cylinder 3.
causes: Failing ignition coil or fouled spark plug on cylinder 3 (petrol)
Low mechanical compression or burnt valve
fixes: Swap ignition coil from cylinder 3 to another cylinder to see if the code follows
Inspect spark plug / injector sealing washer
Perform compression test if misfire stays on the same cylinder

P0304.title: Cylinder 4 Misfire Detected
P0304.meaning: Combustion misfire counted above threshold on cylinder 4.
causes: Failing ignition coil or fouled spark plug on cylinder 4 (petrol)
Low mechanical compression or burnt valve
fixes: Swap ignition coil from cylinder 4 to another cylinder to see if the code follows
Inspect spark plug / injector sealing washer
Perform compression test if misfire stays on the same cylinder

P0321.title: Engine Speed Sensor (G28) Implausible Signal
P0321.meaning: Erratic or missing tooth pulses from crankshaft speed sensor G28.
causes: Metallic debris on G28 sensor tip
Damaged crankshaft tone wheel / rear main seal magnetic ring
fixes: Inspect G28 connector near oil filter housing / bellhousing
Remove G28 to check for swarf or physical contact with the tone ring

P0322.title: Engine Speed Sensor (G28) No Signal
P0322.meaning: ECU receives no crankshaft rotation pulses during cranking or running.
causes: Broken wire in front engine loom
Damaged rear main seal magnetic encoder ring
fixes: Verify live RPM moves above ~200 RPM while cranking
Check 3-pin G28 plug and wiring

P0335.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Circuit
P0335.meaning: Electrical fault in crankshaft sensor G28.
causes: Damaged G28 wire near starter/oil cooler
fixes: Inspect G28 harness and sensor

P0336.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor A Range / Performance
P0336.meaning: Irregular tooth count from crankshaft tone ring.
causes: Bent/corroded magnetic rear main seal ring
Starter interference from weak earth strap
fixes: Clean gearbox-to-chassis earth strap and inspect G28/tone ring

P0340.title: Camshaft Position Sensor A Circuit (Bank 1)
P0340.meaning: Open or short on camshaft Hall sensor G40.
fixes: Check 3-pin G40 plug, 5V/12V supply, and ground

P0341.title: Camshaft Position Sensor (G40) Range / Performance
P0341.meaning: Camshaft Hall sensor G40 pulses are noisy or out of sync.
fixes: Inspect G40 wiring behind timing belt cover
Verify mechanical timing before condemning sensor

P0380.title: Glow Plug / Heater Circuit A Fault
P0380.meaning: Glow plug control module J179 reported an electrical fault in the pre-heat system.
causes: One or more open-circuit glow plugs
Failed J179 glow plug relay module
Blown glow-plug strip fuse in engine bay E-box
fixes: Measure individual glow plug resistance (note: beware 4.4V/5V low-voltage plugs—do not jump directly to 12V!)
Check main supply fuse to J179 relay

P0381.title: Glow Plug / Heater Indicator Circuit
P0381.meaning: Instrument cluster glow-plug lamp control fault.
fixes: Scan 0x17 Instrument Cluster

P0400.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation (EGR) Flow Fault
causes: Vacuum or electrical fault at EGR actuator
fixes: Inspect EGR valve movement and clean carbon deposits

P0401.title: EGR Flow Insufficient
P0401.meaning: Fresh airflow did not drop as expected when the ECU commanded the EGR valve open.
causes: Heavy carbon/oil sludge blocking EGR passages or cooler matrix
Stripped internal gears on electric EGR actuator
Blanked EGR pipe without matching software
fixes: Inspect and clean EGR valve and intake entry port
Run EGR output test / basic adaptation

P0402.title: EGR Flow Excessive
P0402.meaning: Exhaust gas is leaking into the intake when the EGR valve should be closed.
causes: EGR pintle held open by a chunk of carbon
Weak EGR return spring or stuck-open cooler bypass
fixes: Remove EGR valve to check whether the valve seats fully closed

P0403.title: EGR Control Circuit Malfunction
P0403.meaning: Electrical drive or H-bridge fault on the EGR valve motor/solenoid.
causes: Water/coolant ingress inside combined EGR valve & cooler electronics (common on 2.0 TDI CFCA/CAAC)
Seized EGR valve overloading motor driver
fixes: Pop the plastic cap off the EGR actuator to check for moisture, rust, or stripped gears
Verify 12V/5V supply and ground at the EGR multi-plug

P0404.title: EGR Control Circuit Range / Performance
P0404.meaning: EGR position sensor cannot reach its commanded target or closed adaptation stop.
causes: Carbon buildup stopping full valve closure
Worn position potentiometer inside EGR unit
fixes: Check live EGR specified vs actual % position
Clean or replace EGR unit and run adaptation

P0407.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit Low
P0407.meaning: EGR potentiometer signal fell below minimum voltage.
causes: Shorted potentiometer track inside EGR module
fixes: Check 5V supply on EGR connector
Inspect internal EGR electronics for moisture

P0408.title: EGR Sensor B Circuit High
P0408.meaning: EGR potentiometer signal exceeded upper voltage limit.
causes: Open sensor ground in EGR harness
fixes: Test ground wire at EGR plug
Replace EGR assembly if internal track is open

P0420.title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P0420.meaning: Downstream oxygen sensor switches nearly as fast as upstream, showing low oxygen storage in the catalytic converter.
causes: Exhaust flex-pipe or manifold leak upstream of post-cat O2 sensor
fixes: Check exhaust flex joint and flange gaskets for soot marks before condemning the cat
Compare upstream and downstream O2 waveforms at warm cruise

P0441.title: EVAP Emission System Incorrect Purge Flow
P0441.meaning: Charcoal canister purge flow failed self-check.
causes: Sticking N80 EVAP purge valve (test: shouldn't blow through when unplugged)
fixes: Unplug N80 valve and test whether air blows through—if open unpowered, replace N80

P0455.title: EVAP System Large Leak Detected
P0455.meaning: Gross pressure/vacuum leak in fuel tank vapour system.
fixes: Check fuel cap seal and N80 purge valve

P0480.title: Fan 1 Control Circuit
P0480.meaning: Radiator cooling fan 1 PWM control or power fault.
causes: Water-damaged fan controller built into main fan hub
Shared fuse blown by shorted intake flap
fixes: Check engine bay fuses and large 4-pin fan connector under radiator

P0489.title: EGR Control Circuit Low
P0489.meaning: EGR actuator driver circuit shorted low or open.
causes: Seized EGR cooler motor blowing fuse or driver
fixes: Inspect EGR multi-plug and engine bay actuator fuse

P0490.title: EGR Control Circuit High
P0490.meaning: EGR H-bridge current or voltage exceeded upper limit.
causes: Jammed EGR valve drawing high stall current
fixes: Check whether EGR valve shaft moves freely or is seized with soot

P0501.title: Vehicle Speed Sensor Range / Performance
P0501.meaning: Vehicle speed signal received by ECU is missing or erratic.
causes: CAN speed message fault from ABS module
fixes: Scan ABS module (0x03) for individual wheel speed sensor faults

P0507.title: Idle Air Control RPM Higher Than Expected
P0507.meaning: Warm idle speed stayed above target.
causes: Vacuum leak / torn PCV diaphragm drawing air into manifold
fixes: Clamp or test PCV breather hose to see if idle drops

P0520.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor / Switch Circuit
P0520.meaning: Electrical fault in oil pressure switch circuit.
causes: Broken single-wire plug at oil filter housing
fixes: STOP if red oil lamp is active until mechanical oil pressure is verified with a gauge; inspect switch plug

P0522.title: Engine Oil Pressure Sensor Low
P0522.meaning: Oil pressure sensor voltage below minimum.
causes: Low oil pressure or failed oil pressure transducer
fixes: Verify mechanical oil pressure with a workshop gauge before running engine

P0544.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0544.meaning: Electrical fault on pre-turbo EGT sensor 1 (G235).
causes: Open-circuit EGT probe due to thermal cycling
fixes: Measure EGT sensor resistance at the 2-pin bulkhead plug (~200 Ω cold on PT200 probes)
Check cold engine EGT live reading

P0545.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0545.meaning: Short to ground on pre-turbo EGT sensor 1.
fixes: Inspect G235 lead behind turbo

P0546.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0546.meaning: Pre-turbo EGT sensor G235 reads open circuit.
causes: Failed G235 probe in exhaust manifold
Unplugged brown/black 2-pin EGT connector on bulkhead
fixes: Unplug G235 connector and measure probe continuity; open circuit confirms failed probe

P0560.title: System Voltage Malfunction
fixes: Clean and tighten battery posts and chassis grounds

P0562.title: System Voltage Low
P0562.meaning: ECU Terminal 30/15 voltage dropped below threshold.
causes: Failing alternator or slipping auxiliary belt
fixes: Check battery voltage at rest (>12.4V) and charging (~14.0–14.4V)

P0563.title: System Voltage High
fixes: Measure battery voltage running; replace regulator immediately if >15.2V

P0568.title: Cruise Control Set Signal Malfunction
P0568.meaning: Implausible switch state from the indicator-stalk cruise control buttons.
causes: Tarnished sliding PCB contacts inside the left steering-column stalk
fixes: Clean cruise stalk rocker/slide switch contacts with contact cleaner or replace stalk

P0571.title: Brake Switch A Circuit Malfunction
P0571.meaning: Implausible correlation between dual brake pedal switch contacts (disables cruise control and flashes glow plug light on many TDIs).
causes: Failed brake light switch or master-cylinder Hall sensor
Both brake light bulbs blown or incompatible non-ballasted LEDs fitted
fixes: Check whether all rear brake lights illuminate cleanly
Inspect brake pedal switch / master cylinder sensor

P0601.title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
causes: Failed/incomplete ECU tune or low-voltage write interruption
fixes: Have ECU flash integrity checked

P0606.title: ECM / PCM Processor Fault
P0606.meaning: Internal microcontroller monitoring check tripped inside the engine ECU.
causes: Water ingress in ECU plenum / scuttle tray
fixes: Inspect ECU multi-plugs for moisture or green pin corrosion
Verify battery and ECU ground points

P0627.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Open
P0627.meaning: Open circuit to electric lift pump or J538 fuel pump module.
causes: Failed J538 pump controller on top of tank
fixes: Check fuel pump fuse and power at J538 module

P0641.title: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit Open
P0641.meaning: Shared 5V sensor reference bus A inside the ECU is overloaded or pulled to ground (often triggers cascading sensor codes).
causes: Shorted sensor sharing 5V rail A (commonly EGR, MAP, AC pressure, or rail pressure sensor)
fixes: Watch 5V rail A voltage while unplugging sensors on that rail one at a time until 5.0V returns

P0642.title: Sensor Reference Voltage A Circuit Low
P0642.meaning: ECU 5V reference bus A is pulled below ~4.7V by an external short.
causes: Water-damaged EGR, DPF pressure, AC pressure, or boost sensor dragging down the shared 5V rail
fixes: Unplug suspect 3-pin/5-pin sensors one by one while monitoring live 5V reference

P0651.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Open
P0651.meaning: Shared 5V sensor reference bus B is open or shorted.
causes: Shorted sensor on 5V rail B (throttle body, pedal channel 2, cam/crank, or turbo position sensor)
fixes: Isolate by unplugging sensors on rail B one at a time until 5V recovers

P0652.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Low
P0652.meaning: 5V sensor supply rail B pulled low by a shorted sensor.
causes: Shorted throttle, turbo position, or cam/crank sensor
fixes: Unplug rail-B sensors one by one while watching 5V reference

P0670.title: Glow Plug Control Module Circuit
P0670.meaning: Power or control fault at J179 glow plug relay.
fixes: Check heavy fuse feeding J179 and inspect relay pins

P0671.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit Fault
P0671.meaning: Glow plug control unit detected open circuit or abnormal current on cylinder 1 glow plug (Q10).
causes: Burnt-out glow plug in cylinder 1 (Note: check if cylinder 3 uses a PSG pressure-sensing glow plug before ordering)
fixes: Unclip cap on cylinder 1 and test resistance to engine block (~0.5–1.5 Ω typical on steel/ceramic low-voltage plugs)
Apply penetrating oil on a warm engine and use a torque wrench when removing glow plugs to avoid snapping

P0672.title: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Circuit Fault
P0672.meaning: Glow plug control unit detected open circuit or abnormal current on cylinder 2 glow plug (Q11).
causes: Burnt-out glow plug in cylinder 2 (Note: check if cylinder 3 uses a PSG pressure-sensing glow plug before ordering)
fixes: Unclip cap on cylinder 2 and test resistance to engine block (~0.5–1.5 Ω typical on steel/ceramic low-voltage plugs)
Apply penetrating oil on a warm engine and use a torque wrench when removing glow plugs to avoid snapping

P0673.title: Cylinder 3 Glow Plug Circuit Fault
P0673.meaning: Glow plug control unit detected open circuit or abnormal current on cylinder 3 glow plug (Q12).
causes: Burnt-out glow plug in cylinder 3 (Note: check if cylinder 3 uses a PSG pressure-sensing glow plug before ordering)
fixes: Unclip cap on cylinder 3 and test resistance to engine block (~0.5–1.5 Ω typical on steel/ceramic low-voltage plugs)
Apply penetrating oil on a warm engine and use a torque wrench when removing glow plugs to avoid snapping

P0674.title: Cylinder 4 Glow Plug Circuit Fault
P0674.meaning: Glow plug control unit detected open circuit or abnormal current on cylinder 4 glow plug (Q13).
causes: Burnt-out glow plug in cylinder 4 (Note: check if cylinder 3 uses a PSG pressure-sensing glow plug before ordering)
fixes: Unclip cap on cylinder 4 and test resistance to engine block (~0.5–1.5 Ω typical on steel/ceramic low-voltage plugs)
Apply penetrating oil on a warm engine and use a torque wrench when removing glow plugs to avoid snapping

P0684.title: Glow Plug Control Module to PCM Communication Range
P0684.meaning: Diagnostic feedback wire between J179 glow plug relay and engine ECU carries an invalid signal.
causes: Corroded J179 relay socket under battery/E-box
fixes: Inspect J179 relay pins for green corrosion
Verify power and ground feeds to J179

P0685.title: ECM / PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Open
P0685.meaning: ECU cannot energize main power relay coil.
fixes: Inspect E-box main power relay and socket under bonnet

P068A.title: ECM / PCM Power Relay De-Energized Too Early
P068A.meaning: Main ECU power relay (J317) dropped out before the ECU completed its post-shutdown EEPROM save.
causes: Ageing main ECU power relay in E-box
fixes: Test battery state of health; replace J317 main power relay if code recurs with a healthy battery

P0700.title: Transmission Control System (MIL Request)
P0700.meaning: Gearbox ECU requested Check Engine lamp illumination.
fixes: Check Address 0x02 for the specific gearbox fault

P0715.title: Input / Turbine Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0715.meaning: Gearbox input shaft speed sensor fault.
fixes: Scan 0x02 Transmission live input RPM

P0722.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
fixes: Inspect 0x02 Transmission live data

P0726.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Range / Performance
P0726.meaning: Mechatronic unit received an implausible engine speed signal.
fixes: Check Engine (0x01) for G28 crankshaft sensor faults first

P0841.title: Transmission Fluid Pressure Sensor / Switch A Range
P0841.meaning: Hydraulic accumulator pressure in 7-speed dry-clutch DSG (DQ200) failed to build or hold pressure.
causes: Cracked aluminium hydraulic accumulator housing inside DQ200 mechatronic
fixes: Check mechatronic hydraulic pressure in live data; accumulator housing repair kits address cracked threads

P1556.title: Charge Pressure Control: Negative Deviation
P1556.meaning: Boost pressure failed to reach requested target (KWP/early TDI equivalent of P0299).
causes: Split vacuum hose to VNT capsule
fixes: Inspect all push-fit boost hose lugs and seals for oil misting
Vacuum-test VNT actuator and supply lines

P1557.title: Charge Pressure Control: Positive Deviation
P1557.meaning: Boost pressure overshot target threshold and triggered protective fuel cut / limp mode.
causes: Coked VNT vanes inside exhaust turbine housing
fixes: Check VNT lever movement for sticky spots
Verify N75 vents vacuum cleanly when de-energized

P1602.title: Power Supply Terminal 30: Voltage Too Low
P1602.meaning: Unswitched permanent battery supply to the ECU dropped or was disconnected.
causes: Weak battery voltage collapse while cranking
fixes: If battery was recently disconnected, clear code and confirm it does not return

P164B.title: Oil Pressure Switch Malfunction
P164B.meaning: Implausible state on two-stage oil pressure switch (open when running or closed with engine off).
causes: Oil leaking through switch diaphragm into 1/2-pin plug
fixes: Inspect oil pressure switches on filter block; verify mechanical oil pressure

P164D.title: Reduced Oil Pressure Switch Malfunction
P164D.meaning: Low-stage oil pressure switch implausible (common on MQB EA288/EA888).
causes: Low oil pressure at hot idle
fixes: Test actual hot-idle oil pressure with mechanical gauge and inspect switch

P1735.title: Clutch 1 Position Sensor Electrical Malfunction
P1735.meaning: Hall position sensor for odd-gear clutch K1 inside DSG mechatronic failed (common on DQ500 / DQ381).
causes: Failed K1 pressure/position Hall sensor on mechatronic PCB
fixes: Verify gear loss on odd gears (1, 3, 5, 7); specialist mechatronic sensor replacement or unit repair required

P1736.title: Clutch 2 Position Sensor Electrical Malfunction
P1736.meaning: Hall position sensor for even-gear/reverse clutch K2 inside DSG mechatronic failed.
causes: Failed K2 sensor on mechatronic board
fixes: Verify loss of even gears (2, 4, 6, R); repair or replace mechatronic sensor board

P17BF.title: Hydraulic Pump Play Protection Active
P17BF.meaning: DQ200 hydraulic pump ran continuously without reaching cut-out pressure, triggering thermal protection.
causes: Internal hydraulic leak at cracked accumulator seat
fixes: Inspect mechatronic for hydraulic oil leaks from breather and check pump run cycle

P189C.title: Function Restriction Due to Insufficient Pressure Build-Up
P189C.meaning: DSG mechatronic could not build sufficient hydraulic pressure to engage clutches cleanly.
causes: Cracked accumulator mount or leaking internal seal in DQ200 mechatronic
fixes: Diagnose alongside P0841 / P17BF; pressure loss requires mechatronic hydraulic repair

P2002.title: Diesel Particulate Filter Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P2002.meaning: Measured differential or post-DPF pressure/PM indicates gas bypassing or abnormal flow across the DPF.
causes: Cracked internal ceramic DPF monolith (check tailpipe inside for black soot—a healthy DPF tailpipe is clean)
Split or detached G450 differential pressure hose
Low-pressure EGR cooler clogged with soot (MQB EA288)
fixes: Wipe inside the exhaust tailpipe: heavy black soot indicates a cracked DPF core
Inspect rubber hoses to the DPF differential pressure sensor
On MQB 2.0 TDI, check low-pressure EGR cooler flow restriction

P2004.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2004.meaning: Swirl-flap actuator reports the intake flaps remain open when commanded closed.
causes: Broken linkage rod between V157 motor and flap shaft
fixes: Inspect swirl-flap arm and ball-joint linkage
Clean carbon deposits or fit travel-stop repair bracket if over-traveling

P2006.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2006.meaning: Intake manifold runner flaps failed to open when requested under load.
causes: Detached actuator arm or failed flap motor
fixes: Actuate flap linkage by hand to check for binding
Inspect electrical plug on manifold flap motor

P2015.title: Intake Manifold Flap Position Sensor Range / Performance
P2015.meaning: Swirl-flap position feedback voltage went outside its calibrated end-stop window.
causes: Worn plastic mechanical stop on 2.0 TDI manifold allowing the V157 motor arm to over-rotate
Heavy soot deposits on intake flaps
Internal potentiometer wear in flap motor
fixes: Inspect the manifold flap lever stop—on common-rail 2.0 TDI manifolds an aluminium stop bracket restores the rest angle
Clear code and run manifold flap basic setting if supported

P2031.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
fixes: Check resistance across EGT S2 2-pin plug

P2032.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
fixes: Inspect sensor routing near DPF

P2033.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2033.meaning: Open circuit on EGT sensor 2 (pre-DPF / post-turbo).
fixes: Measure probe resistance at its 2-pin connector; replace probe if open

P2047.title: Reductant (AdBlue) Injector Circuit Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P2047.meaning: Open circuit on N474 AdBlue dosing injector.
causes: Unplugged or heat-damaged wire at exhaust AdBlue injector
fixes: Measure N474 coil resistance (~12 Ω) and inspect exhaust underbody plug

P2048.title: Reductant (AdBlue) Injector Circuit Low
P2048.meaning: Short to ground on AdBlue injector N474.
fixes: Inspect underfloor SCR wiring loom

P2049.title: Reductant (AdBlue) Injector Circuit High
P2049.meaning: Short to positive on AdBlue injector N474.
fixes: Test N474 wiring to SCR/ECU

P207F.title: Reductant (AdBlue) Quality Performance
P207F.meaning: NOx conversion or tank quality sensor indicates improper AdBlue fluid.
fixes: Drain and refill with fresh ISO 22241 AdBlue and clean dosing nozzle

P2080.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Range / Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2080.meaning: Pre-turbo EGT sensor G235 reports an implausible temperature compared to adjacent EGT probes after cold soak.
fixes: Compare all EGT sensors (S1–S4) cold before starting engine; the outlier sensor is faulty

P2084.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Range / Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2084.meaning: EGT sensor 2 reading disagrees with neighbouring exhaust temperature sensors.
fixes: Compare cold-soak live EGT readings across all exhaust probes

P2085.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
fixes: Inspect 2-pin plug and replace intermittent probe

P20EE.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EE.meaning: Downstream NOx sensor detects insufficient NOx reduction across the SCR catalyst.
causes: Crystallized AdBlue blocking the N474 dosing injector
fixes: Unbolt AdBlue injector from exhaust pipe and inspect for white urea crystals; clean with warm water
Check AdBlue fluid concentration with a refractometer (target 32.5% urea)

P2100.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Open
P2100.meaning: Open circuit in the intake manifold throttle / anti-shudder valve (J338) motor.
causes: Blown engine bay fuse (often shared with radiator fan module when intake flap shorts!)
fixes: Check engine bay fuse box (commonly a 10A/15A fuse blows when oil enters the throttle flap PCB)
Unplug J338 and inspect for black engine oil pouring out of the connector

P2101.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Range / Performance
P2101.meaning: Intake throttle plate could not reach commanded angle.
causes: Heavy soot/EGR sludge jamming throttle plate
fixes: Remove intake flap housing, clean carbon, and inspect internal plastic gears

P2102.title: Throttle Actuator Control Motor Circuit Low
P2102.meaning: Short or overload in the intake throttle / shut-off flap motor.
causes: Engine oil leaking past throttle shaft seal onto internal PCB
fixes: Check engine bay fuse and inspect J338 connector for oil contamination

P2122.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor D Circuit Low
fixes: Check 6-pin accelerator pedal connector

P2127.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor E Circuit Low
fixes: Check whether P0651/P0652 is also stored; inspect pedal plug

P2138.title: Throttle / Pedal Position Sensor D/E Voltage Correlation
P2138.meaning: Dual safety tracks inside the accelerator pedal module disagree.
causes: Water ingress in footwell pedal plug or plenum bulkhead connector
fixes: Inspect accelerator pedal 6-pin connector and scuttle plenum connectors for moisture

P2146.title: Fuel Injector Group A Supply Voltage Open
P2146.meaning: ECU lost electrical drive capability for injector bank A (often stalls engine immediately).
causes: Piezo injector shorted internally to body/ground, tripping ECU bank shutdown
Chafed injector harness wire shorting to cylinder head
fixes: Unplug injectors one by one and test insulation resistance from each pin to injector body
Inspect injector loom where it enters or crosses the cylinder head

P2149.title: Fuel Injector Group B Supply Voltage Open
P2149.meaning: ECU shut down injector bank B due to an open circuit or short on one of its paired injectors.
causes: Shorted piezo/solenoid injector on bank B
fixes: Test each bank-B injector for pin-to-body short
Check harness continuity between ECU and injector plugs

P2196.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased / Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2196.meaning: Wideband upstream lambda probe reports persistently rich exhaust gas.
causes: Boost hose leak on diesel causing rich mixture under load
Contaminated or aged LSU wideband lambda sensor
fixes: Check charge pipes for boost leaks first on TDI engines
Verify live lambda response during overrun fuel cut (should swing lean cleanly)

P2200.title: NOx Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2200.meaning: Electrical/CAN fault in upstream NOx sensor.
fixes: Check 12V supply and CAN lines at NOx box

P2201.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range / Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2201.meaning: Upstream NOx sensor module reports implausible NOx or O2 values.
causes: Water ingress in underfloor NOx control box
fixes: Inspect underbody NOx module mounting and CAN/power plug

P2202.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2202.meaning: Electrical supply or internal fault on NOx sensor 1.
fixes: Verify battery voltage and ground at the NOx module 4/5-pin plug

P2209.title: NOx Sensor Heater Sense Circuit Range (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2209.meaning: NOx sensor internal ceramic heater fault.
causes: Moisture thermal shock cracking NOx sensor tip
fixes: Replace failed NOx sensor assembly

P2263.title: Turbocharger / Supercharger Boost System Performance
P2263.meaning: Bi-turbo or variable-geometry boost control did not track target across changeover or steady load.
causes: Leaking vacuum changeover valve or reservoir on BiTDI engines
fixes: On BiTDI engines, vacuum-test both actuator capsules and changeover solenoids
Inspect charge cooler and hoses for boost leaks

P2279.title: Intake Air System Leak
P2279.meaning: Unmetered air or pressure loss detected between MAF, turbocharger, and intake manifold.
causes: Split PCV breather hose or torn PCV diaphragm
Leaking rocker-cover or oil filler cap seal
fixes: Smoke-test intake and crankcase breather hoses
Check PCV valve membrane for tears

P229F.title: NOx Sensor Circuit Range / Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P229F.meaning: Downstream post-SCR NOx sensor reports implausible readings (blocks DPF/SCR readiness).
causes: Soot or urea fouling on sensor tip
fixes: Check live NOx ppm during warm overrun decel (should drop near zero)

P242A.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P242A.meaning: Electrical fault on pre-DPF EGT sensor 3 (G495)—active DPF regeneration will be inhibited while present.
fixes: Fix promptly so the DPF does not overload while regeneration is blocked
Test probe resistance at its connector

P242B.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Range / Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P242B.meaning: EGT sensor 3 (G495) reading is implausible compared to exhaust model.
fixes: Check all EGT values after overnight cold soak; replace drifted probe

P242D.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P242D.meaning: Open circuit on pre-DPF EGT sensor 3 (G495).
fixes: Unplug G495 and confirm open circuit with ohmmeter; replace probe

P2452.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit
P2452.meaning: Electrical fault in DPF pressure sensor G450 circuit.
fixes: Inspect 3-pin plug and sensing hoses at G450
Adapt replacement sensor if replaced

P2453.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Range / Performance
P2453.meaning: G450 differential pressure is non-zero with engine off or implausible vs exhaust flow.
causes: Condensation water or ice trapped in G450 sensing hoses
fixes: Check differential pressure with ignition ON, engine OFF (should be ~0 hPa)
Blow clear both stainless/rubber sensing pipes and replace G450 if offset remains

P2454.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P2454.meaning: G450 signal voltage dropped below minimum.
causes: Short to ground on G450 signal or 5V rail
fixes: Measure 5V supply and ground at G450 plug

P2455.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P2455.meaning: G450 signal voltage stuck high / open ground.
fixes: Check G450 connector latch and ground wire

P2456.title: DPF Differential Pressure Sensor Intermittent
P2456.meaning: Erratic readings from G450 DPF pressure sensor.
fixes: Blow hoses dry and replace G450

P2458.title: DPF Regeneration Duration
P2458.meaning: An active DPF regeneration cycle ran longer than allowed without reducing soot load sufficiently.
causes: Boost leak causing excess soot during regen
fixes: Verify live coolant temperature reaches ~88–90°C on road cruise
Check EGT sensors and charge hoses

P2459.title: DPF Regeneration Frequency
P2459.meaning: DPF regenerations are triggering at abnormally short mileage intervals.
causes: High ash load in high-mileage DPF
