Boost leak or worn injectors creating excess soot
fixes: Check oil ash volume and inspect boost pipes before cleaning/replacing DPF

P2463.title: DPF Soot Accumulation Excessive
P2463.meaning: Measured or calculated soot mass in the DPF exceeded the normal road-regeneration threshold.
causes: Repeated short trips aborting active regenerations
Underlying boost leak, EGR fault, glow plug fault, or stuck-open thermostat
fixes: Resolve any other engine/thermostat/EGT codes first
Check actual vs measured soot mass (g) before attempting a service regeneration—never force regeneration above safe soot limits

P246E.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 4)
P246E.meaning: Electrical fault in post-DPF EGT sensor 4 (G648).
fixes: Inspect underfloor EGT 4 cable and test probe resistance

P2563.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Range / Performance
P2563.meaning: Position sensor on the turbo VNT actuator (G581) disagrees with commanded vacuum/duty position.
causes: Perforated vacuum diaphragm inside electronic-feedback turbo capsule
fixes: Apply hand vacuum directly to the turbo capsule—if it will not hold vacuum, replace the capsule
Check live VNT position voltage from rest to full vacuum

P2564.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit Low
P2564.meaning: Turbo actuator position sensor (G581) voltage fell below minimum.
causes: Damaged wire on the 3-pin plug atop the turbo actuator
fixes: Check heat-exposed wiring behind the cylinder head leading to the turbo capsule
Verify 5V supply and ground at the 3-pin actuator plug

P2565.title: Turbocharger Boost Control Position Sensor Circuit High
P2565.meaning: Turbo actuator position sensor (G581) voltage is stuck high / open circuit.
causes: Open ground wire in actuator harness
fixes: Confirm the 3-pin plug on top of the turbo vacuum unit is latched
Test continuity of all 3 wires back to the ECU loom

P261A.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Open
P261A.meaning: Electric auxiliary / EGR / charge-air coolant pump (V188 / V400) reported an open circuit or stall.
causes: Failed electric auxiliary water pump (extremely common on 2.0 TDI CR & BiTDI)
Corroded 3-pin plug at bottom front of engine
fixes: Inspect the 3-pin connector on the electric auxiliary coolant pump behind the radiator/sump
Replace stalled electric pump to restore EGR/intercooler cooling and allow DPF regens

P261C.title: Coolant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P261C.meaning: Auxiliary electric coolant pump PWM diagnostic line pulled low (stalled rotor or electronics fault).
causes: Seized impeller inside V188 electric coolant pump
fixes: Verify 12V, ground, and PWM wire at the auxiliary pump; replace pump if power/ground are good

P2711.title: Unexpected Mechanical Gear Disengagement
P2711.meaning: Gear selector fork slipped out of engagement or failed to engage cleanly.
causes: Selector fork magnet contaminated with metallic swarf
fixes: Inspect DSG fluid condition and run clutch/gearbox basic setting only if mechanical health is confirmed

U0001.title: High-Speed CAN Communication Bus Fault
U0001.meaning: Powertrain high-speed CAN bus entered bus-off or fault state.
causes: Water-damaged module pulling powertrain CAN rails out of spec
fixes: Measure termination resistance across CAN-H and CAN-L with battery disconnected (~60 Ω expected across two 120 Ω terminators)

U0100.title: Lost Communication with Engine Control Module (ECM/PCM)
U0100.meaning: Expected periodic CAN frames from 0x01 Engine ECU timed out.
causes: Blown supply fuse or missing Terminal 15/30 feed to 0x01 Engine ECU
Damaged CAN-High / CAN-Low twisted pair or corroded hinge/underfloor splice
0x01 Engine ECU unplugged or powered down during work
fixes: Check whether 0x01 Engine ECU responds directly in a Full Auto-Scan
Verify fuse supply and ground to the missing module
If recorded intermittently after battery work, clear and re-scan

Verify fuse supply and ground to the missing module

0x03 ABS / ESP unplugged or powered down during work

causes: Blown supply fuse or missing Terminal 15/30 feed to 0x19 Diagnostic Gateway

U0151.title: Lost Communication with Restraints (Airbag) Module
U0151.meaning: Expected periodic CAN frames from 0x15 SRS Airbags timed out.
causes: Blown supply fuse or missing Terminal 15/30 feed to 0x15 SRS Airbags

U0401.title: Invalid Data Received from ECM / PCM
U0401.meaning: This module received an error flag inside a CAN frame sent by the Engine ECU (symptomatic knock-on code).
causes: Active fault stored in 0x01 Engine ECU causing torque/speed signal substitution
fixes: Scan and resolve faults in 0x01 Engine Control Module first; U0401 clears once the engine fault is fixed

U0415.title: Invalid Data Received from ABS Control Module
U0415.meaning: ABS/ESP flagged wheel-speed or stability data as invalid on CAN.
causes: Wheel speed sensor or steering angle fault in 0x03 ABS
fixes: Check 0x03 ABS Brakes for the root sensor fault

U0428.title: Invalid Data Received from Steering Angle Sensor
U0428.meaning: Steering angle sensor G85 broadcast an uncalibrated or implausible angle.
causes: Battery was disconnected and G85 needs lock-to-lock initialization
fixes: Start engine, turn steering full left, full right, and drive straight briefly to re-initialize G85

U1011.title: Supply Voltage Too Low
U1011.meaning: Module supply voltage dropped below normal CAN operating window.
causes: Low 12V battery or cranking voltage dip
fixes: Test resting and cranking battery voltage

U1111.title: Function Limitation Due to Missing Message
U1111.meaning: A feature in this module is disabled because a required CAN frame from another module is absent.
causes: Mismatched long coding enabling an option whose hardware/module is not fitted
fixes: Check recent coding changes or Gateway installation list for non-existent equipment

U1113.title: Function Limitation Due to Fault Value Received
U1113.meaning: Another ECU on the bus reported a fault and substituted a fallback value—this module is healthy and only reacting.
causes: Upstream fault stored in Engine (0x01), ABS (0x03), BCM (0x09), or HVAC pressure sensor
fixes: Read faults in the other scanned modules—fixing the primary sensor fault clears U1113 automatically

U1121.title: Databus Missing Message
U1121.meaning: Expected CAN/LIN message was not received within timeout.
causes: Incorrect coding bit enabled for absent equipment
Disconnected LIN slave (e.g. rain sensor, alternator, blower, alarm siren)
fixes: Cross-check coding changes or inspect LIN bus slave connectors

U1122.title: Databus Implausible Message
U1122.meaning: Received bus frame contained an out-of-range or error-flagged signal.
causes: Companion ECU has an active sensor fault
fixes: Resolve primary faults in companion modules first

U1123.title: Databus Error Value Received
U1123.meaning: Another controller transmitted a 'signal invalid' flag over CAN—this is a secondary knock-on code.
causes: Fault stored in another module (commonly Engine, ABS, or Radar)
fixes: Fix the root fault in the originating module rather than replacing this module

U1400.title: Function Restriction Due to Insufficient Voltage
U1400.meaning: Module disabled high-draw functions (e.g. heated screens, Start/Stop, HVAC) due to low battery voltage.
causes: Short journeys with heavy electrical load
fixes: Charge or load-test 12V battery and verify alternator charging voltage
